item.title: Paper: Mapping and Measuring the Behavioral Evolution of Large Language Models
item.description: The authors developed a method to quantify and track how LLM behaviors diverge or converge over time, helping practitioners understand model evolution beyond simple leaderboard scores.

item.title: Paper: Self-Knowledge Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Patent Matching
item.description: This framework improves patent matching accuracy by using a self-knowledge RAG approach, avoiding the high costs and performance degradation associated with traditional fine-tuning.

item.title: Paper: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
item.description: This method allows GUI agents to improve their visual grounding capabilities post-deployment through an automated reflection loop, enabling adaptation to new interfaces without human feedback.

item.title: Paper: Hierarchical Empirical-Bayes Naive Bayes: Minimax Smoothing and Calibration with AODE Extension
item.description: The researchers introduced an adaptive smoothing method for Naive Bayes that automatically adjusts to data characteristics, significantly improving classification performance on complex tabular datasets.

item.title: Paper: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
item.description: Researchers discovered that encrypted reasoning traces from LLM APIs can be intercepted and reused across sessions, posing a significant security risk for proprietary model architectures.

item.title: Paper: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
item.description: This framework helps data scientists identify and manipulate specific visual features within multimodal models, providing better control over how these systems interpret and process images.

item.title: Paper: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution for LLM Agents
item.description: The authors propose a framework that treats agent safety as an evolving system, learning safe boundaries dynamically from execution trajectories rather than relying on static, hard-coded rules.

item.title: Paper: Agentic Auto-Research is Fuzz Testing
item.description: This paper reframes autonomous research agents as fuzzers, suggesting that tracking execution coverage provides more reliable feedback than standard generate-and-rank methods for complex research tasks.

item.title: Paper: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
item.description: The researchers developed a benchmark to identify and fix common statistical errors made by LLM agents when performing automated data analysis and hypothesis testing.

item.title: Paper: An End-to-End Agent Auditing Engine
item.description: This paper introduces a systematic framework for auditing and evaluating the performance of LLM-based agents, helping developers build more reliable and robust deployment pipelines.

item.title: Paper: Strategy-first synthesis planning for complex natural products
item.description: The authors propose a new strategy-first approach to automated chemical synthesis that mimics human planning, overcoming limitations in existing tools that rely solely on reaction databases.

item.title: Paper: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
item.description: SkillProx improves how LLM agents refine their procedural knowledge by using a gradient-inspired feedback loop to better manage and consolidate reusable task skills.

item.title: Paper: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
item.description: This paper introduces a retrieval-augmented approach for time series forecasting, allowing models to improve accuracy by referencing similar historical patterns from external datasets.

item.title: Paper: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
item.description: The authors created a multi-agent system that automates clinical feature engineering by linking electronic health records to medical guidelines, significantly reducing manual data preparation time.

item.title: Paper: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
item.description: This study evaluates and improves how LLMs handle complex, rule-heavy professional documents, providing a framework for automating quality reviews of technical standards.

item.title: Paper: QuanTiMedAI: Quantum-Enhanced Time-Series Model guided by Agentic AI for Cardiac Arrest Mortality Prediction
item.description: This framework combines quantum-inspired computing with agentic AI to better predict cardiac arrest mortality by analyzing the full temporal progression of patient health data.

item.title: Paper: Spoken Function Calling: A New Perspective on Spoken Language Understanding for Large Audio Language Models
item.description: This paper introduces a structured approach for audio-based AI agents to execute specific functions directly from speech, improving their ability to handle open-domain tasks without complex manual rules.

item.title: Paper: The Effect of Perceived Race and Gender on Police Language Use: Experimental Evidence from VR Simulations
item.description: Researchers used VR simulations to measure how police officers' language patterns change based on the perceived race and gender of virtual characters, providing a causal framework for bias analysis.

item.title: Paper: Teaching Nemotron Greek: Mining a Corpus, Adapting Retrieval, and Grounding Generation for Modern Greek across Specialist Domains
item.description: The authors adapted a retrieval-augmented generation stack for Modern Greek, demonstrating that simple keyword-based methods often outperform complex multilingual dense retrievers in specialized domains.

item.title: Paper: DASyR-LLM: Domain-Aware Symbolic Regression with LLMs for Kinetic Model Discovery
item.description: This framework integrates LLMs into symbolic regression to ensure that data-driven kinetic models for chemical engineering remain physically plausible and scientifically interpretable.
